concepts.def: Kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, etc.
Energy moved between stores mechanically, electrically, by heating or radiation.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.
Useful energy out ÷ total energy in (always less than 100%).
Energy transferred when a force moves an object; W = Fd.
The rate of energy transfer (watts); P = E ÷ t.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Renewables won't run out: solar, wind, hydro, tidal, wave, biomass, geothermal.

Non-renewables will run out: coal, oil, natural gas, nuclear fuel.

Non-renewables are often cheap and reliable but release CO2 or radioactive waste.

Efficiency tells you how much energy is useful and not wasted.

A modern LED bulb is about 90% efficient.

An old filament bulb was only 5% efficient - the rest came out as wasted heat!

Efficiency = useful energy out / total energy in.

A Sankey diagram shows energy flow with arrows.

The width of each arrow = amount of energy.

Useful energy goes one way (often right), wasted energy splits off (often down).

The total width going in always equals the total going out - that's conservation!

mcqs.q: Why are infrared cameras used to detect warm objects in the dark?
options: Warm objects emit infrared radiation due to their temperature; the camera detects this emission.
Atoms emit only one colour each, determined by their temperature.
Infrared cameras shine infrared light onto objects so they reflect back visibly.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.

mcqs.q: Why do atoms emit light only at specific wavelengths rather than a continuous spectrum?
options: Atoms can emit any wavelength, but only certain ones are visible.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
Atoms emit only one colour each, determined by their temperature.
Electrons occupy discrete energy levels; transitions between levels emit photons of specific frequencies (E = hf).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Energy store”?
options: Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Kinetic store”?
options: Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.

Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.
